theme.styleGuide:
Ember Launch is a builtin QoderWork AI Slides visual reference. Match its deep-charcoal pitch-deck scheme, confident scale, and warm, human, ambitious tone while using the bundled Alibaba PuHuiTi 3.0 font stack for generated slides.
Reference typography cues: display: Sora; heading: Sora; body: Inter; mono: Space Mono; serif_cn: Noto Serif SC; sans_cn: Noto Sans SC. Treat these font names as visual cues, not external font dependencies.
Color language: a deep charcoal-brown canvas (#141210) with slightly warmer surface panels (#1D1A16), warm white type (#FAF6F0) for everything readable, and a single ember-orange family (primary #F97316, accent #FB923C) reserved for the emotional beats — hero numbers, emphasis words, hairline rules, and the ask. Warmth is the whole point; the orange is used sparingly so it stays hot.
Best for: Consumer product and lifestyle brand pitch decks, D2C and food/beverage ventures, community-driven products, and launch keynotes that need warmth and human connection. The charcoal field keeps the deck grounded and confident while ember-orange accents carry the beats that matter.
Reference notes: A founder-in-the-room pitch system — every slide sits on the same deep charcoal-brown field, lit as if by embers rather than fluorescent light. Sora carries all display and heading type: heavy weights, tight tracking, oversized on the cover and on the single hero number that anchors the market-size and traction slides. Inter handles body and leads in a quiet supporting voice. Space Mono provides the deck chrome — the kicker labels, page numbers, and the company wordmark that repeats in the corner of every slide, so the deck always reads as one continuous keynote. The ember-orange (#F97316 warming to #FB923C) is disciplined: it touches only the numbers you want remembered, the one emphasized word inside a headline, the 32px accent rule under a kicker, and the call-to-action on the closing ask. Dividers on the dark field are 1px hairlines at low foreground opacity — structure you feel more than see. There are no drop shadows and no gradients except one restrained ember glow behind the cover title and the ask, like warmth radiating from the center. The mood is a late-evening launch talk: dark room, warm light, a person telling you why this matters.

decorativePatterns.name: visual-system
decorativePatterns.description:
Deep charcoal canvas warmed by ember-orange accents and warm white type — a dark consumer-brand pitch deck built for warmth and ambition.
Every slide shares one deep charcoal-brown field (#141210) with slightly warmer surface panels (#1D1A16); warm white type (#FAF6F0) does all the reading work and drops to a muted warm grey (#B7AEA4) for secondary copy.
The ember-orange family (primary #F97316, accent #FB923C) is the only chromatic color in the system and is rationed on purpose. It appears exclusively on: the single hero number that anchors the market-size and traction slides, one emphasized word inside a headline, the 32px accent rule beneath a kicker, list counter marks, and the closing call-to-action. Used any more freely it stops reading as embers and starts reading as a warning label.
Sora is the structural face — heavy display weights with tight tracking, sized huge on the cover and on hero numbers so the deck has real pitch-stage presence. Inter recedes into body and lead roles. Space Mono is the chrome voice: kicker labels, page counters, and the repeating company wordmark pinned to a corner of every slide, giving the deck a single continuous keynote identity.
Depth is flat and warm. No drop shadows, no rounded-corner cards fighting the field; borders are 1px hairlines at low warm-white opacity, present as faint structure rather than dividers. The single indulgence is one soft ember radial glow behind the cover title and the ask slide — warmth radiating from the center of an otherwise still, dark room. Motion is zero; slides do not transition.
**Key Characteristics:** one deep charcoal field on every slide; ember-orange rationed to the beats that matter; oversized Sora numbers with pitch-stage presence; mono chrome and a repeating corner wordmark tying the deck into one keynote.
